evidence: Nominal arithmetic passes and matches the frozen template: task.toml:18/21/27 sets agent 7200s, build 600s and verifier 13200s; each gates judge.toml:4 is 600s and scored functional/polish/visual are 9000/900/900s. test.sh:207 serializes judges with --max-concurrent-agent 1; gate total 1200 <1500, scored total 10800 <11100, and suite budgets 1500+11100=12600 <13200 (600s outside-suite margin). However the liveness deadline is not a wall-clock bound. tests/test.sh:50 and :138 call urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=2).read(); :116-121 and :171-176 merely repeat that blocking call 120 times with 0.25s sleeps. A response that keeps delivering bytes can hold one read beyond the nominal socket timeout; there is no enclosing absolute readiness deadline. The restart helper has an outer 55s timeout (restart_mcp.py:11,39), while its purported 30s readiness loop can itself overrun that bound. The current raw index explicitly admits unchanged_shared_liveness_control. I verified all six artifact hashes plus source-binding.json, and current task and template test.sh both hash bd68259276ca4b034654efc8a1723a4e702ed62dbe590af6201565f43eabe5aa, matching its binding. The pinned-image bounded control measured timeout=2 with a successful read lasting 3.518818652984919s (RESULTS.json SHA256 f201fdc5ecc336ae92c44285ba60f6c764d889b32cf1a9ac360e3afd166e19b6; stdout.log SHA256 d36003783f6e57ade35849660b8142eec6195827d56fc5116d7a8ca8bee63f94). This confirms the timeout semantics, not an actual 55s/13200s harness overrun. Separately, adequacy of the configured judge/build workload remains NOT EXERCISED: raw-evidence-index.json lists Full configured judge completion/workload as not_measured and runtime-evidence.json is absent. The 79-criterion functional scripted golden passed in 140.066s; its functional/prompt hashes match the frozen candidate, but direct Playwright duration cannot establish LLM judge completion within 9000s. The agent-image build succeeded in 2.761889s, but build-stderr.log shows both apt and npm layers CACHED, so this is not the required realistic cold build measurement. All 102 current_golden, 14 current_agent_image, 21 current_installer_control and six liveness artifact hashes were verified without mismatches. Index SHA256: 72d4525c76e152dc665b42eb21462e41ac3c5d9bb007090c99302e8ee444ef6e. No provider or new runtime/security probe was executed.
counterexample: A broken server sends successful health headers and one body byte every 0.5s without finishing its response. The readiness .read() keeps receiving progress, so the 2s socket timeout need not fire and the advertised readiness bound is absent; the outer verifier budget can be consumed before judges begin. The bounded eight-byte control confirms the prerequisite behavior only; no indefinite/full-harness run is claimed. For the broken-app-pass challenge, a prompt finite health response with a dead Run/save UI is explicitly rejected by the authored-marker render gate and clean-context write/read constraints gate, so I found no false pass from timeout values alone. For a conforming alternative, a fully working app with different UI/dialog structure requires the judge to discover controls and perform the complete shared protocols; it could be cut off at 9000s despite satisfying the public product request. No configured run establishes or refutes that risk, and the scripted golden cannot do so.
suggested_fix: Have the shared-harness owner resolve the liveness deadline defect through the authorized canonical-template process using an absolute deadline and bounded health-response handling, then freeze/review the resulting candidate; do not patch this task locally to silence QC. Obtain hash-bound full configured judge timing and realistic cold-build evidence before clearing row 11. Keep current budgets until a measured workload reason supports an explicitly recorded authorized change below five hours.
